title: Use `mapToDouble(Employee::getSalary).summaryStatistics()` to get count/sum/min/max/avg in one pass.
shortTitle: Use mapToDouble(...).summaryStatistics() to get count, sum, min, max, avg in one pass
keyPoints: summaryStatistics() computes count, sum, min, max, and average in a single pass over the stream
Returns DoubleSummaryStatistics for DoubleStream, IntSummaryStatistics for IntStream, LongSummaryStatistics for LongStream
For an empty stream, count and sum are 0, average is 0.0, min is Double.MAX_VALUE, max is Double.MIN_VALUE
Always check getCount() before trusting getMin() and getMax() on potentially empty streams
Collectors.summarizingDouble() produces the same object inside a groupingBy for per-group statistics
One traversal for five figures is the efficiency gain interviewers want to hear

s1_definition.oneliner: summaryStatistics() computes count, sum, min, max, and average together in a single traversal of the stream.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **summaryStatistics()** is a terminal operation on a primitive stream that returns a statistics object.
- **DoubleSummaryStatistics** holds count, sum, min, max, and average computed in one pass.
- **IntSummaryStatistics** and **LongSummaryStatistics** serve IntStream and LongStream respectively.
- **Collectors.summarizingDouble()** produces the same statistics object inside a collect, useful as a downstream in groupingBy.
s1_definition.analogy: Instead of running through the salary ledger five separate times to get the head count, total, smallest, largest, and average, Priya at the National Bank of India makes one pass and fills in all five boxes on a summary slip at once.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  List<Employee>
  [Rajesh:75K, Priya:82K, Amit:68K, Kavita:91K, Neha:78K]
       │
       │  .mapToDouble(Employee::getSalaryAsDouble)
       ▼
  DoubleStream [75000, 82000, 68000, 91000, 78000]
       │
       │  .summaryStatistics()   (single pass)
       ▼
  ┌──────────────────────────────────┐
  │   DoubleSummaryStatistics        │
  │   count   = 5                    │
  │   sum     = 394000.0             │
  │   min     = 68000.0              │
  │   max     = 91000.0              │
  │   average = 78800.0              │
  └──────────────────────────────────┘
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
When a payroll report needs several numeric figures together, computing each with its own stream traverses the data multiple times. Instead, project salaries into a primitive DoubleStream with mapToDouble and call summaryStatistics(), which makes a single pass and returns a DoubleSummaryStatistics object holding count, sum, minimum, maximum, and average all at once.

This pairs well with Collectors.summarizingDouble() inside a groupingBy to compute per-department statistics in one pass. At the National Bank of India, one traversal for five figures is exactly the efficiency gain the dashboard team needed.

The trap to watch for is empty-stream behaviour: count, sum, and average are zero, but min and max come back as sentinel values (Double.MAX_VALUE and Double.MIN_VALUE). Always check getCount() before trusting the extremes.

Remember one sentence: summaryStatistics() gives count, sum, min, max, and average in one pass, and always check count before trusting min and max on an empty stream.
